newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-KARLSRUHE UPSET LEVERKUSEN IN NEW COMPETITION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KARLSRUHE UPSET LEVERKUSEN IN NEW COMPETITION.

text.p: Karlsruhe beat last season's Bundesliga runners-up Bayer Leverkusen on penalties in the first match of the new, lucrative German League Cup tournament on Friday.
The teams were equal 2-2 after 90 minutes and Karlsruhe won the shoot-out 6-5. There was no extra time.
Karlsruhe, sixth in the league, will play Stuttgart, fourth, in a semifinal on Tuesday.
The competition, involving the top six finishers in last season's Bundesliga, is the opener to the new season which starts on August 2.

Cup winners Stuttgart qualified automatically for the semifinals like champions Bayern Munich, who will play either European champions Borussia Dortmund or VfL Bochum in the other semifinal on Wednesday. Dortmund and Bochum meet on Sunday.
Karlsruhe earned one million marks ($550,000) for their victory. The winners of the final on July 26 will receive 2.5 million marks ($1.4 million) even before playing their first league match.
New signing Stefan Beinlich, who joined from Hansa Rostock, put Leverkusen in front after five minutes but two minutes later, Karlsruhe equalised through Burkhard Reich.
Striker Ulf Kirsten, last season's league top scorer with 22 goals, made it 2-1 for Leverkusen in the 21st minute but South African-born striker Sean Dundee levelled nine minutes from time.
Karlsruhe keeper Claus Reitmaier gave his side the edge in the shoot-out by blocking an effort from Carsten Ramelow.
